scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Semah is rooted in the Alevi-Bektaşi tradition, a belief system centered on admiration for Ali, the fourth caliph.
It has been practiced for centuries as part of the Cem ritual.
In 2010, the Semah was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Semah is performed during the Cem ceremony as one of twelve mandatory services.
It symbolizes the spiritual journey of humanity, the cycle of life, and the unity of all creation with God.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers move in circular paths and rotate around their own axes.
The right hand is held palm-up, and the left hand is held palm-down.
Movements alternate between slow and fast, often imitating the flight of a crane.
Watch for Turnalar semahı.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The primary instrument is the saz, a long-necked lute.
The music is defined by the aksak rhythm, a complex meter characteristic of the region.
Listen for the saz.
The pulse is Aksak.
The music is driven by the rhythmic, plucked strings of the saz, which provides a melodic and percussive foundation for the vocal chanting of spiritual poetry.

narration: Forms include the turnalar semahı (crane dance) and the kırklar semahı (dance of the forty).
Part of the broader Sufi tradition of Sama, though distinct in its Alevi-Bektaşi context.
